Cline CLI is an autonomous coding agent for interactive terminal sessions.
Roomote is not yet publicly available. Here's what former Roo Code users are choosing right now.

Cline: set API Provider to Ollama, base URL http://localhost:11434, pick a model. Ollama's page says use a context window of at least 32K for coding; Cline's own docs name no number but advise enabling Use Compact Prompt (Settings, Features), keeping tasks focused and starting a new task when context grows.
When launched through `ollama launch cline`, Ollama sets Cline's provider to Ollama, points it at the local Ollama endpoint, and selects the model you choose.

Roo Code automatically defers to the Modelfile's num_ctx setting by default. When you use a model with Ollama, Roo Code reads the model's configured context window and uses it automatically. You don't need to configure context size in Roo Code settings - it respects what's defined in your Ollama model.

Cause If no model instance is running, Ollama spins one up on demand. During that cold start it may allocate a larger context window than expected. The larger context window increases memory usage and can exceed available VRAM or RAM. This is an Ollama startup behavior, not a Roo Code bug.

Continue configures Ollama in a YAML config (~/.continue/configs/config.yaml) via model blocks (uses: ollama/<model>), model: AUTODETECT, or manual provider: ollama with apiBase and roles. It does not auto-pull: a missing tag returns 404 until you run ollama pull with the exact tag.

Ensure the model's context window is pinned Save your Ollama model with an appropriate num_ctx (via /set + /save, or preferably a Modelfile). Roo Code automatically detects and uses the model's configured num_ctx - there is no manual context size setting in Roo Code for the Ollama provider.

Ollama's VS Code integration is the Ollama extension from the VS Code Marketplace, surfacing models in the Chat model picker; it needs VS Code 1.127 or newer and finds models at http://127.0.0.1:11434 by default. Ollama 0.17.6+ is recommended for cloud sign-in.

For local models in VS Code, Ollama's docs say to set context length to at least 64k in Ollama Settings and reload the window; VS Code may display a model's maximum context while Ollama allocates less at runtime. This is a larger floor than Cline's 32K recommendation.

Roo Code (while maintained) used Ollama's native API, read num_ctx from the Ollama model rather than setting it in the editor, and could run out of memory on first request because Ollama may allocate a larger context than expected. Fixes: pin num_ctx via Modelfile, preload with ollama run, use smaller quantizations, clear stale processes with ollama ps / ollama stop.

An open-source Apache 2.0 AI coding agent for VS Code. Good choice for developers who prefer a simpler single-agent workflow without specialized agents. Kilo Code vs Cline comparison

1. Open Roo Code in VS Code and click the **gear icon** on the top right corner of the Roo Code window to open **Provider Settings** 2. Set `API Provider` to `Ollama` 3. (Optional) Update `Base URL` if your Ollama instance is running remotely. The default is `http://localhost:11434` 4. Enter a valid `Model ID` (for example `qwen3` or `qwen3-coder:480b-cloud`. See all supported models [here](https://ollama.com/search)) 5. Adjust the `Context Window` to at least 32K tokens for coding tasks

Earlier VS Code versions do not reliably cancel requests from language model providers. Ollama 0.17.6 or newer is recommended for cloud model sign-in and richer model metadata. Older versions may still work with local models.

1. Install the [Ollama extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=Ollama.ollama) from the VS Code Marketplace. 2. Open Chat in VS Code. 3. Open the model picker at the bottom of the chat input. 4. Choose a model from the **Ollama** section.
Roo Code founder Matt Rubens announced the project would archive. The Roo Code extension had accumulated 3M+ VS Code installs.

Roo Code archived its repository on May 15, 2026. The team behind it is now building a new product called Roomote. If you used Roo Code or are evaluating Roomote, here's what happened and what your best options are today.

JetBrains IDEs connect to Ollama via the AI chat sidebar: Set up Local Models, Third Party AI Providers, Ollama, Host URL http://localhost:11434. Ollama's page says a JetBrains AI Subscription is required.
Cline against Ollama cloud: enable Use custom base URL, set https://ollama.com, enter an ollama.com API key, and choose a cloud model that supports tool calling.

Across editors, remote Ollama needs the client's base URL changed from localhost; Continue also needs OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 on the server, and Roo's docs flag the base URL change for other machines.

Zed configures Ollama under language_models.ollama with api_url, auto_discover (default on), and available_models entries (name, display_name, max_tokens, supports_tools, supports_thinking, supports_images). Remote Ollama (cloud) uses api_url https://ollama.com plus an API key or OLLAMA_API_KEY.

Zed sends context length to Ollama as num_ctx with a default of 4096 tokens; raise it globally with context_window or per model with max_tokens. External Agents, terminal threads and Edit Prediction are configured separately.

Continue's Ollama guide warns agent mode needs tool support, which some models (e.g. DeepSeek R1) report as unsupported even with capabilities: [tool_use]; Continue may default to a large context causing memory errors, so lower contextLength. The guide was written against Ollama v0.11.x and Continue v1.1.x, so details may be dated.
If you're looking for an alternative, check out ZooCode (a fork started by the Roo Code community) and Cline (from where Roo Code originated).
Roo Code behavior: Roo automatically uses whatever num_ctx is configured in your Ollama model

1. Open Cline settings > `API Configuration` and set `API Provider` to `Ollama` 2. Select a model under `Model` or type one (e.g. `qwen3`) 3. Update the context window to at least 32K tokens under `Context Window`

Zed requests to Ollama include context length as the num_ctx parameter. By default, Zed uses 4096 tokens.
Continue may use a higher default context length than other tools. Reduce contextLength in your config (e.g., to 2048), or try a smaller model. See Ollama provider troubleshooting for details.
